summary: Separate the visible glowing surface of a practical fixture from the mechanism that illuminates nearby receivers, then tune them under one declared exposure.
objective: A lamp, sign or screen reads as luminous while nearby surfaces receive intentional light from a declared runtime light, baked field or probe rather than an assumed emissive-material side effect.
applies_when: A visible emissive mesh should appear to light a room or nearby prop.
Blender reference lighting must be approximated in a Three.js runtime.
intent_signals: make an emissive screen light nearby objects
balance a visible bulb and its area light
stop neon from clipping without darkening room
example_prompts: Build a neon sign with a visible emissive tube and a separately inspectable receiver-light mechanism.
Match a softbox prop using an emissive panel plus a RectAreaLight or a baked contribution.
negative_signals: Raising emissiveIntensity and assuming every neighboring material will receive more light.
Tuning the visible emitter and exposure independently until the receiver mechanism is unknowable.

principles: Visible emission and received illumination are separate responsibilities in a standard Three.js material/light setup. Name both owners even when Blender rendered them as one authored fixture.

Choose a receiver mechanism per need: direct runtime light for movement, baked indirect illumination for static scenes, or a reviewed probe/other renderer feature. Distinguish Blender's visible Emit surface pass from indirect receiver lighting caused by emissive objects; excluding Emit alone does not establish that bounced emissive illumination was excluded. Do not silently enable several copies.
Tune in a controlled order: lock exposure and reference materials, set receiver illumination, then set visible emissive color/intensity and any separate post effect.
implementation: In Blender, name the emitter mesh and any reference light separately. If baking, record visible Emit, direct and indirect contribution controls separately; do not use the Emit toggle alone as the ownership test for emissive light bounced onto receivers.

In Three.js, bind emissive/emissiveMap with the documented color space, then create and aim the declared receiver light or bind the bake/probe. When choosing RectAreaLight, use a supported PBR material and initialize the backend-specific LTC data: RectAreaLightUniformsLib for WebGLRenderer, or RectAreaLightTexturesLib with RectAreaLightNode.setLTC for WebGPURenderer. Do not infer an area light from the mesh automatically.
Provide emitter-only and receiver-only toggles plus a neutral diffuse card at known positions; keep exposure fixed during the comparison.
observable_checks: With receiver lights disabled, the fixture remains visibly emissive while the neutral card loses that mechanism’s illumination.
Moving a runtime practical changes receiver illumination; a baked practical remains visibly static and is labeled accordingly.
Highlights and bright emitter detail remain readable under the declared tone mapping/exposure, without using exposure changes to conceal ownership errors.

creative_affordances: Practical fixtures may be neon, screens, magical runes, furnace mouths or stylized panels.
Receiver-light shape and falloff may be art directed after the mechanism is declared.
known_limits: MeshStandardMaterial emission alone is not a general GI solver.
RectAreaLight support, materials and shadows vary; the cited current class does not cast shadows.
No Blender light transport, Three.js light, tone mapping or render was run.

claims.statement: MeshStandardMaterial emissive is a material color unaffected by other lighting; emissiveMap is color data typically tagged SRGBColorSpace and is modulated by emissive color and intensity.
claims.scope: Three.js visible material emission; it does not establish illumination of other objects.

source_refs.locator: Color textures and working color space

claims.statement: Three.js RectAreaLight is a separate rectangular light with no shadow support; current documentation limits it to PBR materials and requires backend-specific LTC initialization through RectAreaLightUniformsLib for WebGLRenderer or RectAreaLightTexturesLib with RectAreaLightNode.setLTC for WebGPURenderer.
claims.scope: Current Three.js direct-light mechanism; pin and verify the installed backend/revision and initializer imports.

source_refs.locator: Important Notes and Code Example: PBR-only, no shadows, and backend-specific LTC initialization

claims.statement: Blender Cycles exposes an Emit bake type for material surface emission and a selectable Emit contribution in Combined baking alongside separate direct and indirect lighting controls; therefore the bake configuration, not the Emit label alone, determines the retained lighting product.
claims.scope: Blender bake controls only. The documented Emit surface term must not be conflated with indirect illumination received after light from an emissive object bounces.
